cause: The body graph's temb input is [6, 3k, 5376] and the heads graph's [k, 2688], with k (the step's distinct row timesteps) dynamic in 1...3 (Scripts/export-h3-profile.py). T2VA passes k = 1 at step 0 (video and audio both at t = 1.0) and k = 2 afterwards (the shift-12 and shift-3 schedules diverge); FL2VA passes 2 and then 3 (keyframe rows at max(t, 0.999)). Core AI specializes a reshape-enabled function once per input shape and keeps every specialization until the model is released, so the k change at step 1 added a second body specialization.
fix: H3ModulationPadding (Sources/AetherH3CoreAI/H3ProfileStages.swift): every step's AdaLN tables and timestep embedding are padded to the trajectory's largest k by repeating existing rows, so a render uses one body and one heads specialization. Exact because the block reads its table only through index_select on the AdaLN indices (< 3k) and the heads read temb rows only through the timestep indices (< k). No re-export. A workaround for Core AI's per-shape retention, not a fix of it.

stepTime: The extra table rows cost nothing measurable: steps 1-7 use the k = 2 (T2VA) or k = 3 (FL2VA) specialization in both builds; the padded build no longer specializes again at step 1.
step0Transient: Both memory-gate renders of T2VA 960x544 showed a transient Metal rise in step 0: run 1 twice to 16.12 GiB (t+12 s and t+28.6 s into the step, about 5 s each), run 2 once to 14.05 GiB (t+13 s), each released in pieces back to the 10.5 GiB level. In run 1 footprint stayed near 11.1 GiB (allocated, untouched). No transient appeared in the standalone repeat, the fresh-cache render, the gate's other three renders, or the current-build render. Cold Core AI specialization does not reproduce it; the cause is not known. The gate keeps run 2, so measured admission covers a 14.05 GiB denoising peak.

memoryGate.admissionNote: This gate's entry (14.49 GiB) kept only the second T2VA 960x544 render and does not cover the first render's 16.12 GiB transient; the next gate carries it (--carry-peaks), for an admitted worst case of about 16.6 GiB, higher than the unpadded build's 15.26 GiB. Padding lowers the steady plateaus and the video-decode footprint, not the admission.
